The method is designed to produce a substrate suitable for epitaxial growth that exhibits a high degree of biaxial crystal orientation while suppressing or preventing the formation of irregular portions. By improving the crystal alignment of the substrate surface, the method enables the formation of high-quality epitaxial layers on the substrate.

In this method, a metal base material is laminated with a copper layer having a face-centered cubic (fcc) rolling texture. The lamination is performed by surface-activated bonding, in which the bonding surfaces of the metal base material and the copper layer are activated before being joined. This technique allows the copper layer to be firmly bonded to the metal base material without relying on processes that could disturb the crystal orientation or generate undesirable irregularities at the bonded interface.

After the copper layer has been laminated onto the metal base material, the surface of the copper layer is mechanically polished. This polishing step removes surface roughness, defects, and other imperfections that may have been introduced during lamination or handling. As a result, the copper layer is provided with a smoother and more uniform surface, which is advantageous for subsequent crystal orientation control and epitaxial growth.

Following mechanical polishing, the copper layer is subjected to an orientation heat treatment. This heat treatment promotes recrystallization and improves the biaxial orientation of the copper layer. Through this process, the copper layer develops a more highly aligned crystal structure, thereby enhancing its suitability as a template for epitaxial deposition.

The copper layer is laminated under conditions such that specific X-ray diffraction intensity ratios for the (200) and (220) crystal planes are maintained within predetermined ranges before and after lamination. In particular, the relationship between the diffraction intensities associated with the (200) plane and the (220) plane is controlled so that the fcc rolling texture of the copper layer is not significantly degraded by the lamination process. By ensuring that these XRD ratios remain within defined limits, the method preserves the desired crystal texture of the copper layer and contributes to achieving a substrate having a high degree of biaxial crystal orientation without formation of irregular parts.
outputs.L4:
A method is provided for producing an epitaxial-growth substrate having excellent biaxial crystal orientation. The method includes preparing a metal base material and a copper layer, bonding the copper layer to the metal base material by surface-activated bonding, mechanically polishing the surface of the bonded copper layer, and then subjecting the resulting laminate to an orientation heat treatment. Through these steps, the copper layer is caused to develop a highly controlled crystal orientation, thereby forming a substrate surface suitable for subsequent epitaxial growth.

In the surface-activated bonding step, the bonding surfaces of the metal base material and the copper layer are activated, for example by removing surface oxides and contaminants, and the activated surfaces are then brought into contact and bonded. This enables strong bonding at relatively low temperature while suppressing deterioration of the crystal orientation of the copper layer. After bonding, the surface of the copper layer is mechanically polished to reduce surface irregularities and to prepare the layer for the orientation heat treatment. The heat treatment promotes recrystallization and orientation of the copper layer, resulting in a copper surface having improved in-plane and out-of-plane alignment.

In this method, the crystal orientation of the copper layer is controlled using X-ray diffraction orientation ratios. In particular, the copper layer is selected or processed so that its XRD orientation ratio before lamination and its XRD orientation ratio after lamination fall within predetermined ranges. By controlling these orientation ratios, the formation of irregularly oriented portions or defective regions in the copper layer can be suppressed. As a result, the copper layer after heat treatment exhibits high biaxial orientation over a broad area.

The resulting epitaxial-growth substrate includes the metal base material and the highly oriented copper layer bonded thereto. Because the copper layer has a smooth surface and a controlled crystal orientation, it can serve as an effective template for epitaxial growth of functional layers, such as oxide layers, buffer layers, superconducting layers, or other crystalline thin films. The method therefore enables stable production of a highly oriented substrate while reducing defects caused by local orientation disorder, making it useful for manufacturing high-performance epitaxial film products.
outputs.L5:
**The XRD Technique**

The XRD technique, or X-ray diffraction, is an important analytical method used to study the structure of crystalline materials. It works by directing X-rays at a sample and measuring how the rays are diffracted by the atoms inside the material. Because atoms in crystals are arranged in regular patterns, the diffracted X-rays create a unique pattern that can be used to identify phases, measure crystal structure, and determine material properties.

The XRD method is widely used in chemistry, physics, geology, materials science, and engineering. Researchers use it to analyze metals, minerals, ceramics, polymers, and pharmaceuticals. One major advantage of XRD is that it can provide detailed structural information without destroying the sample.

The results of an XRD analysis are usually shown as a diffraction pattern, with peaks appearing at specific angles. Each peak corresponds to a particular spacing between atomic planes in the crystal. By comparing these peaks with reference data, scientists can identify unknown materials and understand their composition.

In modern laboratories, the XRD technique plays a key role in quality control and research. It helps scientists develop stronger materials, improve manufacturing processes, and investigate new compounds. Overall, the XRD method is a powerful tool for understanding the internal structure of matter.

The bonded laminate is optionally heat treated to stabilize or recrystallize the copper layer while retaining biaxial texture. In the resulting substrate, the copper layer provides an epitaxial growth surface in which, as measured by X-ray diffraction, an orientation ratio of a (200) plane, defined as I(200)/ΣI(hkl) for fcc copper diffraction peaks, is not less than 60%, preferably not less than 80%, and an orientation ratio of a (220) plane, defined as I(220)/ΣI(hkl), is not greater than 20%, preferably not greater than 10%. The substrate is thereby suitable for epitaxial formation of buffer layers, oxide films, superconducting films, or semiconductor layers on a mechanically reinforced metal base.

What is claimed is:

1. A method for manufacturing a substrate for epitaxial growth, comprising:

preparing a copper layer having a face-centered cubic crystal structure and a rolling texture;

performing a mechanical polishing treatment to a bonding surface of the copper layer so that a surface roughness is reduced;

subjecting the bonding surface of the copper layer and a surface of a support substrate to surface activation treatment under vacuum atmosphere;

bonding the activated bonding surface of the copper layer and the activated surface of the support substrate by surface-activated bonding, thereby obtaining a bonded body;

performing an orientation heat treatment to the bonded body, so that crystal orientation of the copper layer is arranged for epitaxial growth use,

wherein, in the mechanical polishing treatment and the orientation heat treatment, the rolling texture of the face-centered cubic copper layer is maintained, and formation of an irregular part a3 in the copper layer is suppressed.

2. The method according to claim 1, wherein the mechanical polishing treatment is carried out with a polishing condition which does not give excessive strain to the copper layer, whereby a disturbed crystal region is not substantially generated on the bonding surface side.

3. The method according to claim 1, wherein the orientation heat treatment is performed at a temperature and a time by which recrystallization causing random orientation is avoided, so that the copper layer keeps a {100}<001> cube orientation or a rolling orientation suitable for epitaxial growth.

4. The method according to claim 1, wherein the surface activation treatment includes irradiating an ion beam or an atom beam to the bonding surface of the copper layer and the surface of the support substrate.

5. The method according to claim 1, wherein the support substrate comprises sapphire, silicon, glass, ceramic, or a metal plate having higher rigidity than the copper layer.

Description excerpt:

According to the present invention, a substrate for epitaxial growth can be manufactured by bonding a copper layer to a support substrate by a surface-activated bonding method. Before bonding, the surface of the copper layer is mechanically polished. At this time, the polishing is not performed so strongly that a working affected layer becomes large. Therefore, even after polishing, the fcc rolling texture originally contained in the copper layer remains.

Thereafter, the polished surface of the copper layer and the surface of the support substrate are activated in vacuum, and both surfaces are contacted with each other. Since the activated surfaces have high bonding ability, bonding can be made at room temperature or at a low temperature. Thus, unnecessary thermal influence to the copper layer is small.

After bonding, an orientation heat treatment is carried out. This heat treatment is selected so that orientation of the copper layer becomes suitable as an under layer for epitaxial growth. However, the heat treatment condition is controlled not to cause generation of an irregular part a3. The irregular part a3 is a region where the crystal orientation is locally disturbed or where the rolling texture is broken. When such irregular part a3 is formed, epitaxial growth on the copper layer becomes nonuniform. In the present method, because mechanical polishing, surface activation, bonding pressure and heat treatment temperature are controlled, the fcc rolling texture of the copper layer is maintained continuously, and the irregular part a3 is not formed.

Accordingly, a substrate having a copper layer with stable crystal orientation can be obtained, and an epitaxial film can be grown with good orientation on the copper layer.
